:::{#lem-arithmetic-interval}
#### The intervals of an arithmetic code

In the [arithmetic code](#def-arithmetic-code) for $n$ independent copies of $X$,
the final interval of a message $x = (x_1, \ldots, x_n)$ has width $\pf{x_1} \cdots \pf{x_n}$,
and the final intervals of two different messages do not overlap.

:::

::: {.proof}

Each step replaces an interval of width $b - a$ by a slice of width $(b - a) \pf{x_i}$.
After $n$ steps the width is $\pf{x_1} \cdots \pf{x_n}$.

The slices that the values of $X$ own are the intervals $[F(x), F(x) + \pf{x})$,
which do not overlap,
because each starts where the one before it ends.
So the slices of one interval do not overlap either.

Let $x$ and $x'$ be two different messages,
and let $j$ be the first position where they differ.
Before step $j$,
both messages have the same interval.
At step $j$ they take different slices of it,
which do not overlap.
Later steps keep each interval inside its own slice,
so the final intervals do not overlap.

:::
